First, note that the series can be written as

$$
12{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(n+3)(n+5)}.
$$

We are also given that

$$
\frac{1}{(n+3)(n+5)}=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+3}-\frac{1}{n+5}).
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
12{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+3}-\frac{1}{n+5})=6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n+3}-\frac{1}{n+5}).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{0} & =6[(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5})] \\ {s}_{1} & =6[(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5})+(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6})] \\ {s}_{2} & =6[(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{7})] \\ {s}_{3} & =6[(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{7})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{8})] \\ {s}_{4} & =6[(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{8})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{9})]\end{aligned}
$$

We notice that all of the terms cancel except $\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{4},$ and the $-\frac{1}{N+4}$ and  $-\frac{1}{N+5}$ terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
{s}_{N}=6[\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{N+4}-\frac{1}{N+5}].
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{12}{(n+3)(n+5)} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }6[\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{N+4}-\frac{1}{N+5}] \\  & =6{lim}_{N\to \infty }[\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{N+4}-\frac{1}{N+5}] \\  & =6[\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-0-0] \\  & =6[\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}] \\  & =6\cdot \frac{7}{12} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
